title: A polynomial-uniform certificate for one rank-three field is not a universal gradient result
statement: The earlier rank3 closed-field certificate remains a polynomial-uniform result for its actual field, not all gradients or the positive-definite16 optimum. The new snapshot adds a matched rank3 example whose uniquely weighted fixed original four rays fail the cost budget, while a different six-ray ordinary allocation certifies the SAME field at1/32. Feasible catalogues still give upper bounds and independently ROC-admitted orbits give lower bounds on the all-allocation optimum. Saved brackets report no actual globally ROC negative energy. The full-covariance calibration uses a known non-ROC polynomial and is not a separation.

For failure/repair: the same actual four-wave field and fixed original covariance directions versus a genuinely different positive six-ray allocation. The rank3 example is not the positive-definite16 optimum.

The12-mode covariance-rank4 example compresses21 ordinary atoms to17, with numerator/denominator sizes reaching55715bits. A saved multiplier is directly checked; older serialization failure and interrupted re-inversion remain preserved.
